title: Articles in Context - Definite vs Indefinite
hint: First mention of something usually takes 'a' or 'an'. When you mention it again, use 'the'. Specific or unique things always take 'the'.
passage: Yesterday, I went to @@@1 park near my house. In @@@2 park, I saw @@@3 old man sitting on @@@4 bench. @@@5 man was feeding @@@6 birds with bread crumbs.

gapFeedback.1: Use 'the' if it's a specific park you know, or 'a' if it's any park near your house. Both work here.
gapFeedback.2: Second mention of 'park' - it's now specific, so use 'the'.
gapFeedback.3: 'Old' starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an'.
gapFeedback.4: First mention of 'bench' - use the indefinite article 'a'.
gapFeedback.5: Start of sentence + second mention of 'man' - capitalize 'The'.
gapFeedback.6: First mention of 'birds', but in this context 'the' works because we're referring to the birds that were there at that specific time.

feedback.correct: Perfect! You've correctly used articles throughout the passage. You understand when to use indefinite articles (a/an) for first mentions and definite articles (the) for subsequent references and specific items.
feedback.incorrect: Review your article choices. Remember: first mention = a/an, subsequent mention = the. 'The' is also used for specific or unique things. Check each gap carefully.
